alex.k Hey team — uploaded an nsys timeline from a p99 spike run. Link: https://perf.redwood/trace/2723456789 :eyes:

maria.p Got it. Short summary?

alex.k p99 jumped from 38ms -> 210ms on a 8k seq workload at batch=4. nvtx shows attention kernels interleaving with kv-write commits. The weird bit: write kernels are serialized by a small write-queue on the device.

jonathan Hmm write-queue? You mean our ring buffer for pending KV writes?

alex.k yeah. I annotated NVTX as `KV_WRITE_QUEUE_LEN` in serving runtime. Perfetto slices show bursts where `write_queue_len` hits 12 and we see `flash_attn` fall back to fused variant mid-request.

tsai Can you paste the perf snippet?

alex.k ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=kv_racewalk.nsys 
# then open in perfetto
```

leah On the trace, I see repeated small `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls for the writeback path, each ~7-12us, but the kernel selector waits for writes to drain before starting fused-attn. That serialized a batch of 4 requests. :thinking:

maria.p Does the selector use synchronous checks like `cudaStreamQuery`? That would explain the stalls.

alex.k It calls `stream.synchronize()` in the write path for safety when write_queue_len > threshold. We added that after a correctness bug last quarter.

sudhir That safety net might be too conservative. If the write path only needs ordering, we can change to event-based fence instead of full sync.

jonathan Agree. Also the kernel-selection heuristic prefers fused-attn when kv_reads <= 3 and seq<10k, but it doesn't account for pending writes. So fused selection gets vetoed mid-schedule.

leah Proposed quick fix: short-circuit selection: if write_queue_len > 6 prefer flash variant (which is more tolerant of concurrent writes) and use `cudaEventRecord` fences on write completion.

alex.k I prototyped that locally: patch reduces p99 from 210ms->52ms on the same replay. Throughput back to normal. I pushed diff to branch `perf/racewalk-writequeue`.

maria.p Can you share the diff? Also any regression risk?

alex.k Diff: ```diff --git a/runtime/kernel_selector.cc b/runtime/kernel_selector.cc 
@@ -120,6 +120,12 @@ bool prefer_fused(const Heuristics &h) {
+  if (runtime_metrics.write_queue_len > 6) return false; // avoid fused under heavy writes
+  // keep old heuristics below
```

alex.k Risk: changes when customers intentionally overload writes; flash variant is slower single-threaded but avoids sync stalls. We should add a rollout flag.

tsai Could we instead make selector query `write_queue_latency_ms` and compute expected stall cost vs fused latency? More principled.

sudhir Yes, we can add a micro-benchmark to calibrate fused vs flash under varying write_queue lengths. I can run a sweep overnight (nsys + perfetto captures).

bench-bot Run queued: perf-sweep --workload=8k-seq --batches=1-8 --mode=selector --output=/tmp/sweeps/2723456789.json

leah Nice. Also add telemetry: histogram of `write_queue_len` per model route and tie to rollout gating.

maria.p Once we have numbers, let's do a canary with the short-circuit and event-fence. Add a feature-flag guarded config: `selector.write_queue_veto_threshold` default 6.

alex.k I'll open PR with tests + NVTX annotations and a perf summary in the PR description. Anyone want to pair-review the event-fence code? @tsai @jonathan

jonathan Happy to. I'll look at correctness edge cases for rendezvous ordering.

tsai I'll help with perf story and ensure we don't regress memory pressure.

infra-bot Deploy note: canary window requires dedicated GPU pool and perf hooks enabled. Schedule?

maria.p Start canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC, duration 4 hours, monitoring p50/p95/p99 and write_queue_len histogram. If p99 > baseline*2 rollback.

alex.k Thanks all. I'll drop the nsys + perfetto links and PR when ready. :thumbsup:
